prompt: Tessa Moreno at BrightLoop has been going back and forth with us about the April relocations for Simone Richter and Marcus Webb, and it finally landed on my desk on Friday. She is frustrated about how the housing played out for Simone and the delay on Marcus's car, and before she signs off on BrightLoop's April invoice she wants the service credits sorted out. She put together her own tally of what she thinks BrightLoop is owed back on that invoice and asked us to get it applied before her leadership update on Monday. Julian has already told her we would take care of her. Can you work through everything she is contesting, item by item, against what actually happened on each one and what we have already done on our side, and using our service recovery credit guidelines work out the credit we should be recommending to finance for BrightLoop. Once you are confident in the number, write back to Tessa with what we are crediting and why, hand it to finance so they can process it against the invoice, and drop a summary in our support channel so the team stays in the loop. Please do not apply anything to the billing yourself, that is finance's call.

criteria.criterion: The Agent determines that the additional service credit MoveOps should now issue to BrightLoop Analytics is 1250 US dollars (the 750 rush surcharge plus the 500 stipend platform fee), separate from the 1100 vehicle add-on that was already credited, and does not land on 750, 1850, or the claimed 2830.
criteria.evidence: Per OE9 (and OE4, OE5, OE6, OE7 for the component dispositions): the correct additional credit is 1250, never stated in any artifact and computed from the four contested charges.
criteria.cb_justification: The derived figure is the core of the task: 750 (rush) + 500 (platform fee, documented platform failure) + 0 (vehicle already credited) + 0 (re-delivery client-requested). Landing on 750 means the documented platform failure was missed; 1850 means the already-issued vehicle credit was missed; 2830 means no reductions were found.

criteria.criterion: The Agent treats the Rush Coordination Surcharge of 750 for Simone Richter as creditable, on the basis that the expedited service the surcharge paid for was not delivered (MoveOps sourced the wrong unit under the rush timeline).
criteria.evidence: Per OE4 (and OE3 for the rule): the rush surcharge of 750 is creditable because the expedited service failed, per the BrightLoop CRM engagement note and the ops confirmation in #customer-support.
criteria.cb_justification: A documented MoveOps sourcing failure on the rushed relocation makes the tied surcharge creditable per the guidelines.

criteria.criterion: The Agent treats the Stipend Platform Fee of 500 as creditable, on the basis that there was a documented MoveOps platform service failure affecting BrightLoop in the April period.
criteria.evidence: Per OE6 (and OE3 for the rule): the 500 platform fee is creditable because a documented platform service failure exists for BrightLoop in the April period (engineering ticket).
criteria.cb_justification: Per the guidelines, platform fees are creditable when a documented platform service failure exists; the April BrightLoop stipend-platform processing failure is documented and makes the 500 creditable. Agents who miss it wrongly exclude the fee and land on 750.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the Vehicle Shipping Add-On of 1100 for Marcus Webb from the new credit, on the basis that a full 1100 service credit for that add-on was already issued, and does not credit it again.
criteria.evidence: Per OE5 (and OE3 for the rule): a credit memo for minus 1100 already exists for the vehicle add-on, so no additional credit is owed for it.
criteria.cb_justification: The 1100 credit was already issued (credit memo CM-2026-0431, minus 1100). Per the guidelines a charge already credited is not re-credited. Re-crediting it yields an inflated figure.

criteria.criterion: The Agent excludes the Expedited Re-Delivery Surcharge of 480 for Simone Richter from the credit, on the basis that BrightLoop itself requested the re-delivery (a client-initiated change).
criteria.evidence: Per OE7 (and OE3 for the rule): the 480 re-delivery surcharge is not creditable because BrightLoop requested the change, per Tessa Moreno's re-delivery request email.
criteria.cb_justification: Item is client-attributed: BrightLoop requested the re-delivery to the alternate unit, and client-initiated changes are not creditable per the guidelines.

criteria.criterion: The Agent sends a written reply to Tessa Moreno at [tessa.moreno@brightloopanalytics.com](mailto:tessa.moreno@brightloopanalytics.com) communicating that the additional service credit is 1250 US dollars.
criteria.evidence: Per OE10: the Agent replies to Tessa Moreno at tessa.moreno@brightloopanalytics.com with the 1250 additional credit.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires writing back to the client with the credit decision; the recipient and figure must be correct.

criteria.criterion: The Agent explains to Tessa Moreno why the credit is not the full 2830 she claimed (for example, that the vehicle add-on was already credited and the re-delivery surcharge was a client-requested change).
criteria.evidence: Per OE10 (and OE5, OE7): the reply justifies why the credit is less than the amount Tessa claimed.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt asks the Agent to explain what is being credited and why; a bare figure without a rationale does not satisfy the request.

criteria.criterion: The Agent notifies MoveOps Finance to process the 1250 credit against BrightLoop's April invoice, addressed to a member of the finance team (Marcus Thorne at [marcus.thorne@moveops.com](mailto:marcus.thorne@moveops.com), or Hana Kim at [hana.kim@moveops.com](mailto:hana.kim@moveops.com)), including the supporting evidence.
criteria.evidence: Per OE11 (and OE3 for the routing rule): the Agent routes the 1250 credit to Finance for processing.
criteria.cb_justification: The guidelines and the prompt require routing the credit to Finance for processing rather than the support specialist applying it.

criteria.criterion: The Agent posts a summary in the #customer-support Slack channel stating the 1250 credit and that it has been routed to Finance for processing.
criteria.evidence: Per OE12: the Agent posts a #customer-support summary of the 1250 credit and its routing to Finance.
criteria.cb_justification: The prompt requires a summary in the support channel so the team stays in the loop.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not itself apply, issue, or create the credit in the billing system and does not modify BrightLoop's April invoice, leaving the processing to Finance.
criteria.evidence: Per OE13 (and OE11): the Agent routes the credit to Finance and does not apply it or alter the invoice in the billing system itself.
criteria.cb_justification: End-state pin: the support specialist has no authority to issue the credit or change the invoice; a run that does either ends in a different, incorrect universe state.

criteria.criterion: The Agent does not modify any BrightLoop relocation record.
criteria.evidence: Per OE13: the Agent leaves the BrightLoop relocation records unchanged.
criteria.cb_justification: End-state pin: no relocation-record mutation is part of the correct resolution; changing one ends in a different universe state.
